# TAM

A TAM is a ceiling: what would exist if we won every eligible institution.
It is not a forecast and it is not the number to underwrite. We compute it
three ways so the ceiling can be audited.

## Scenario A - Scenario A - list price (ACV Rs 120,000)

| Method | Kind | Formula | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | CEILING | IIC-bearing institutions x annual contract value | Rs 168.8-196.4 cr |
| M2 | CEILING | India HE technology market (US$ 3,347.2M) x defensible share | Rs 139.7-838.5 cr |
| R | REACHABLE | HEI universe x reachable adoption x our capture x ACV | Rs 1.8-15.8 cr |

Ceiling span between M1 and M2: **6.0x** (within one decade: True).

Ceiling-to-reachable gap: **53.0x**.

## Scenario B - Scenario B - required ACV (ACV Rs 1,027,962)

| Method | Kind | Formula | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | CEILING | IIC-bearing institutions x annual contract value | Rs 1446.0-1682.5 cr |
| M2 | CEILING | India HE technology market (US$ 3,347.2M) x defensible share | Rs 1197.1-7182.7 cr |
| R | REACHABLE | HEI universe x reachable adoption x our capture x ACV | Rs 15.1-135.6 cr |

Ceiling span between M1 and M2: **6.0x** (within one decade: True).

Ceiling-to-reachable gap: **53.0x**.

## Why M1 uses a conflicting population

M1 multiplies the IIC-bearing population - 14,067 to 16,367 institutions - by the ACV.

That population carries conflict C-01: three official sources give three counts. We carry the range and never a single figure. A 16.4% spread in the population input propagates directly into the TAM, which is exactly why the range is shown rather than a midpoint.

## Why M2's share band is 0.5-3%

The share is the entire difficulty of a top-down estimate. 0.5% is the share implied by institutions that demonstrably file innovation returns. 3% is the share implied if every IIC-bearing institution bought a typical academic-systems line item. In Scenario B the band scales by the price ratio, because at a higher price the product must carry a larger share of wallet to produce the same outcome.

## Why R is not a fourth TAM method

R applies an explicit adoption band (5-15% of HEIs) and an explicit capture band (5-15% of that). It is deliberately *not* called a TAM, because it is not a ceiling - it is an estimate of what is winnable. See Triangulation.md for why averaging the two categories is refused.
